spatial_transcriptomics.html: The fastest-growing technology tracked. Papers per 100K works rose about 24x from 2020 to 2025, 89% a year.
Funding followed. NIH dollars went from $54 million in fiscal 2020 to $620 million in 2025, third among the 10 technologies.
Visium is still the most-named platform at 40% of mentions. Xenium, launched in 2022, reached 18% by 2025, the largest gain of any platform here.
spatial_transcriptomics.holds: t.lead == 'Visium' and t.gainer == 'Xenium' and t.gainer_share >= 0.15 and t.gainer_launched >= 2021

spatial_proteomics.html: The second-fastest-growing technology tracked. Papers per 100K works grew 34% a year since 2020, about 4.4x overall.
One platform holds about half of mentions. PhenoCycler (CODEX) has 49%; the next, Hyperion, has 14%.
NIH dollars grew 41% a year, from $20 million in fiscal 2020 to $109 million in 2025.

single_cell.html: The largest body of work outside the mature technologies, 14,823 papers in 2025, and still growing 31% a year per 100K works.
single_cell.holds: t.papers > max(spatial_transcriptomics.papers, spatial_proteomics.papers, long_read_sequencing.papers, ms_proteomics.papers, affinity_proteomics.papers, protein_sequencing.papers) and t.growth > 0.2

single_cell.html: The most NIH funding of any technology tracked, $906 million in fiscal 2025, up from $345 million in 2020.
The most concentrated platform market tracked. Chromium accounts for 82% of platform mentions, down from 92% in 2020.

long_read_sequencing.html: Papers per 100K works more than doubled from 2020 to 2025 (2.3x).
NIH dollars grew faster than papers, 28% a year to $203 million in fiscal 2025.
Nanopore platforms account for 69% of mentions. Within them the mix is moving to higher throughput. MinION fell from 53% in 2020 to 38%, and PromethION rose to 15%.
long_read_sequencing.holds: t.top_vendor == 'Oxford Nanopore Technologies' and t.top_vendor_share > 0.5 and t.lead == 'MinION' and t.lead_share < t.lead_share_from - 0.05 and t.gainer == 'PromethION'

ms_proteomics.html: Papers per 100K works grew 6% a year since 2020, slower than affinity proteomics (13%), which started from a smaller base (269 papers in 2020, against 1,330 here).
Thermo Fisher instruments account for 81% of platform mentions. Within them, Q Exactive fell from 63% in 2020 to 42% as Orbitrap Exploris rose to 16%.
ms_proteomics.holds: t.top_vendor == 'Thermo Fisher Scientific' and t.top_vendor_share > 0.7 and t.lead == 'Q Exactive' and t.lead_share < t.lead_share_from - 0.1 and t.gainer == 'Orbitrap Exploris'

ms_proteomics.html: NIH dollars were roughly flat, $79 million in fiscal 2020 and $82 million in 2025.

affinity_proteomics.html: Papers per 100K works nearly doubled from 2020 to 2025 (1.8x), from a small base of 269 papers.
Two platforms account for 75% of mentions, Olink (40%) and Simoa (34%).
The least NIH funding of any technology tracked, $5 million in fiscal 2025 for grants that name these methods.

protein_sequencing.html: The smallest field tracked, 48 papers in 2025, though papers per 100K works grew 10% a year since 2020.
One commercial platform, Platinum (Quantum-Si), accounts for every platform mention.
About 32% of matched patents use protein sequencing as a readout or one of many applications rather than as the invention, the highest share of any technology tracked.

short_read_ngs.html: Flat as a share of all research, 191.3 papers per 100K works in 2025 and 187.1 in 2020.
NIH dollars and US patent applications both fell since 2020, NIH by 5% a year to $616 million and applications from 134 to 97.
Illumina platforms account for 91% of mentions. NovaSeq rose from 6% in 2020 to 37%, the most-named platform.
short_read_ngs.holds: t.top_vendor == 'Illumina' and t.top_vendor_share > 0.8 and t.lead == 'NovaSeq' and t.lead_share > t.lead_share_from + 0.1

qpcr_dpcr.html: The largest body of work tracked, 31,004 papers in 2025, growing about as fast as research overall (+1% a year per 100K works).
NIH dollars naming these methods fell from $87 million in fiscal 2020 to $63 million in 2025.
No platform dominates. CFX leads with 29% of mentions; QuantStudio about doubled its share since 2020, to 26%.
qpcr_dpcr.holds: t.lead == 'CFX' and t.second == 'QuantStudio' and t.lead_share < 0.35 and t.gainer == 'QuantStudio' and t.gainer_share >= 1.9 * t.gainer_share_from

flow_cytometry.html: Papers per 100K works are flat, but the field is second in NIH dollars ($722 million) and first in US patent applications (99 in 2025).
The least concentrated platform market tracked. The most-named platform, LSR Fortessa / LSR II, has 17% of mentions.
CytoFLEX about doubled its share of mentions since 2020, from 7% to 16%.
